title: Advanced Fleet Optimization
contentStatus: Draft for DiFacto review. Title and content to be confirmed.

sections.title: From Awareness to Active Optimization
learningObjectives: Recall performance metrics introduced in L2-M6
Understand this module's shift from awareness to active optimization work
sections.content: L2-M6 introduced cycle time and throughput as concepts worth being aware of. This module goes further: actively optimizing an existing, operational fleet's performance - tuning routes, timing, and task distribution to extract more throughput from the same physical fleet.

keyTerms.note: The time one full task takes from start to finish.
How much work the fleet completes in a given period.

sections.title: Identifying Optimization Opportunities
learningObjectives: Understand how to identify where optimization effort is worthwhile
Recognize the role of data logging (from L2-M6) in this process
sections.content: Optimization starts with data - the logging introduced conceptually in L2-M6 becomes the actual working material here. Analyzing mission timing, route patterns, and congestion points across a fleet's operational history reveals where genuine inefficiency exists, rather than optimizing based on intuition about where problems might be.

keyTerms.note: A place where units regularly queue or slow each other down.

sections.title: Route Optimization
learningObjectives: Understand general approaches to improving route efficiency
Recognize trade-offs involved in route optimization decisions
sections.content: Route optimization might involve adjusting waypoint placement, reconsidering zone configuration (building on L3B-M3), or restructuring mission sequencing to reduce unnecessary travel. Changes here often involve trade-offs - a route optimized for one scenario may perform worse under different operational conditions, so optimization should be validated against realistic operational variation, not just the ideal case.

sections.title: Task Distribution Optimization
learningObjectives: Understand optimization considerations for how tasks are distributed across a fleet
Recognize the goal of balanced utilization
sections.content: Beyond individual routes, fleet-level optimization considers how tasks are distributed across available units - aiming for balanced utilization rather than some units sitting idle while others are consistently overloaded. This connects to the automatic task assignment introduced in L2-M4, but at this level involves actively tuning the distribution logic rather than relying entirely on default behavior.

keyTerms.note: The share of time a unit spends doing useful work rather than waiting.

sections.title: Measuring Optimization Impact
learningObjectives: Understand how to validate that an optimization change actually improved performance
Recognize the risk of assuming improvement without measurement
sections.content: Any optimization change should be measured against the same metrics used to identify the original opportunity - confirming throughput or cycle time genuinely improved, not just assuming it did because the change seemed logical. Before-and-after comparison using consistent data is what separates genuine optimization from well-intentioned guessing.

sections.title: Preparing for the Capstone
learningObjectives: Understand how this module's skills integrate with the L4B capstone project
Recognize optimization as one component of the broader Advanced Programming competency
sections.content: This module completes the technical skill-building portion of L4B, alongside CNC integration, PLC work, and complex payload configuration. The capstone project (L4B-M5) draws on all of these together - optimization skill specifically supports demonstrating that a capstone solution doesn't just work, but performs well.

questions.question: What does this module add beyond the performance awareness from L2-M6?
options: Active optimization of an operational fleet
A new set of fleet settings that raise MoRo's maximum driving speed
A formal exam on cycle time and throughput measurements
questions.feedback: Correct. This module moves from awareness to active, hands-on optimization.

questions.question: What should optimization efforts be based on?
options: The operators' impressions of which routes feel slowest
The route lengths shown on the facility's original floor plan and layout drawings used at design time
Data on mission timing, route patterns, and congestion across operating history
questions.feedback: Correct. Data-driven analysis reveals genuine inefficiency, rather than guessing.

questions.question: Why should route optimization be validated against realistic operational variation?
options: Variation only matters for routes longer than one zone
A route that is better in one scenario can be worse in others
Realistic variation is only needed for the first route you change
questions.feedback: Correct. Optimization that only suits an ideal case risks underperforming in real conditions.

questions.question: What is the goal of task distribution optimization across a fleet?
options: Giving every unit exactly the same route length each day
Concentrating tasks on fewer units so the rest can charge
questions.feedback: Correct. Balanced utilization across available units is the goal of this optimization.

questions.question: Why measure optimization impact rather than assuming a change helped?
options: Measurement is needed only when the change makes routes longer
Assuming improvement is fine if the change followed good practice
A before-and-after comparison shows genuine improvement rather than a guess
questions.feedback: Correct. Consistent measurement distinguishes genuine optimization from well-intentioned guessing.
